narrative.overview:
The site is an engineer's bound lab notebook. The frame is a green computation pad ruled with a 24px grid; the reading column is a plain sheet laid on top of it, with no grid behind the words. Every entry carries a number in the left margin (E-### for writing, P-### for projects, §n for sections), every page carries a dated signature row, and a revision is shown by striking the old words through in red rather than deleting them.

The system is three inks on one paper: graphite for text and rules, ballpoint blue for what the reader can act on and where the reader is, and a red margin rule that also does strike-through revisions. Everything else is built from square-cornered boxes and 1 to 2px ink lines. There are no shadows, no rounded corners, and no fills beyond the pad, the sheet, and the code panel. Night mode is the same notebook under a desk lamp: a deep green-black pad with chalk-pale ink, the same structure, the same three roles.

Density is moderate and reading-first: 17px body at 1.8 line height on a 68ch measure, with the furniture (field labels, entry metadata, notes) set smaller and quieter around it. State is carried by line form, not by color or badges: dashed underline means draft, double underline means revised, red strike means outdated.
keyCharacteristics: Green grid pad in the frame only; the reading column is gridless sheet.
A single red vertical margin rule at the gutter edge, the only vertical color line on any page.
Margin gutter holds only numbers the reader uses: entry numbers and § section numbers.
Square corners everywhere; borders of 1px (hairline/rule) to 2px (section rules).
Flat: no shadows, no decorative gradients.
One self-drawing pen stroke is the only motion; all other state changes are instant.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Graphite, ballpoint blue, and margin red are the only inks. Any new color is a syntax token inside a code block or it does not ship.

rules.name: The Pen Means Act-or-Here Rule
rules.body: Blue marks something clickable or the reader's current position (active nav, current TOC item, the pen ring). Static decoration in blue is a defect.

rules.name: The Red Is Revision Rule
rules.body: Red is the margin line and the strike-through. A placeholder or sample marker uses a 1px ink frame, not red.

rules.name: The Field Label Rule
rules.body: An uppercase tracked label always names a value printed right beneath it, like a form field on a notebook page. It never floats above a headline as a teaser.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Dates, page numbers, entry numbers, reading times, and counts use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Drawn-Not-Lifted Rule
rules.body: Separation comes from a 1.5px ink border or a change from pad to sheet, never from a shadow or blur. Hover changes a fill (pad to sheet) or an underline, not elevation.

rules.name: The Grid-Is-The-Only-Gradient Rule
rules.body: The pad's 24px grid is built from two hard-stop linear gradients; that is the only gradient in the system. No soft color gradients on fills, text, or borders.

dos: Do keep the 24px grid on the pad frame and put reading text on the gridless sheet.
Do number things in the margin only when the number is real: E-### entries, P-### projects, §n sections.
Do show revisions by striking old text through in red (0.09em on inline text, 2 to 3px on titles), keeping it legible in ink-2.
Do draw every box with square corners and 1.5px ink; use 2px ink for section and page rules.
Do carry state with line form: dashed underline for draft, double underline for revised, red strike for outdated.
Do mark placeholder content with the sample tag: a 1px ink frame, ink-2 text, 13px / 600.
Do use tabular numerals for every date, count, and number.
donts: Don't use rounded corners, drop shadows, or soft color gradients anywhere.
Don't use ballpoint blue on anything that is neither clickable nor the reader's current position.
Don't use margin red for tags, badges, warnings in general, or placeholder markers; it is reserved for the margin rule, strike-through revisions, and the outdated callout border.
Don't put decorative numbers or line numbers in the gutter.
Don't add fades, slides, or entrance animations to content; the pen ring is the only drawn motion and other state changes are instant.
Don't introduce a second display face or set prose in the mono; JetBrains Mono is for code only.
Don't place an uppercase tracked label above a headline as a teaser; labels name a field's value.
